Welcome to the first League Classic community poll. Our goal with these polls is to involve you, the community, in the direction that we take League Classic. Questions in these polls cover two broad types:

Voting can be done in “The Council” tab in the League client and is open for seven days, with the first running from August 26 through September 2. Eligible players may answer each question and change their answers until the poll closes. Each point of voting power gives one vote on each question. We’ll publish the results after voting closes in the Patch Notes.

This first poll covers questions across a few areas: game length, item revivals, and some map features. You can skip questions if you don’t have an opinion about the topic.

title: League Of Legends Worlds 2026 Returns To The U.S. In October. Here Are The Dates And Cities
summary: League Of Legends Worlds 2026 Returns To The U.S. In October. Here Are The Dates And Cities  GameFragger.com
content:
Worlds is coming back to the United States.League of Legends Worlds 2026startsOctober 15inLos Angelesand endsNovember 14atBarclays Center in Brooklyn. This is the first American Worlds since 2022, when the last stages sat in Atlanta, New York, and San Francisco.

The window matters now because the regions that fill the 19-team field are already in their last split. LCK playoffs start this weekend. LPL, LEC, LCP, and the Americas leagues are cutting teams on the same calendar. The next live patch after 26.17 is September 10. After that, the conversation turns into Worlds patch, Worlds skins, and who actually booked a plane. So it is better to get ahead of schedule and be ready for it now, with everything that we know so far.

Play-In isOctober 15 to 18at theRiot Games ArenainLos Angeles. That room holds about 300 people. Four teams play a double-elimination, best-of-five bracket under Fearless Draft. One team leaves L.A. with a Swiss ticket. The other three go home before the real tournament starts.

Swiss and knockouts move to theCredit Union of Texas Event Center in Allen, just north of Dallas. Swiss isOctober 23 to 26andOctober 28 to 31. Quarterfinals areNovember 3 to 6. Semifinals areNovember 7 and 8. The building holds a little over 8,000. This is where most of Worlds actually happens.

The final isNovember 14 at Barclays Center in Brooklyn. Capacity is about 19,000. That is the NBA arena date, the trophy shot, and the only day a lot of casual fans will watch.

Tickets already went throughRiot’s Fan Firstpresale in late July, then general sale. If you do not have one, you are hunting resale or watching the broadcast.

title: Professional gaming is brutal on the body – inside the growing field of treating esports injuries
summary: Professional gaming is brutal on the body – inside the growing field of treating esports injuries  The Conversation
content:
Chinese esports player Jian “Uzi” Zi-hao was more than a star “League of Legends” player: He was so talented that his teamstructured its entire strategy around his abilities, funneling resources to him and another teammate, Shi “Ming” Sen-Ming, so the duo could lead the team to victory. Over the course of his career,he earned more than US$500,000in tournament prize money.

And yet in 2020,Jian announced his retirement, his storied career cut short by chronic wrist and arm injuries.

Video games have a reputation for keeping people glued to the couch. But for those who compete against the best players in the world, gaming can be surprisingly physically and mentally taxing.

The best esports players often have grinding schedules. They’re expected to regularly practice, participate in scrimmages and compete in official matches. Even at the recreational level,esports players cite the mental toll: playing for hours a day, every day, to hone their skills so they can “climb the ladder.”

A 2021 study of Portuguese esports playersfound that 37% experienced anxiety and depression, and 45% experienced sleep disturbances. The most common physical injuries in esports generally fall under eye problems and musculoskeletal issues.

Prolonged screen time leads to many types of vision problems in gamers, from the more common eye fatigue toa decreased ability to focus. Furthermore, the light emitted from screens appearsto contribute to sleep disturbancesby disruptingthe release of melatonin, the hormone that helps regulate your sleep-wake cycle.
